cards.prompt: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
choices: The bus was late; we missed first period.
The bus was late; and we missed first period.
cards.accept: A semicolon replaces the conjunction. With "and" added, the sentence needs a comma instead: "late, and we."

cards.prompt: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
choices: Our team practiced all week, we still lost on Friday.
Our team practiced all week; we still lost on Friday.
cards.accept: Two complete sentences can't be joined with only a comma. That's a comma splice.

cards.prompt: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
choices: The roads were icy, however; school stayed open.
The roads were icy; however, school stayed open.
cards.accept: The semicolon goes before the transition word and a comma after it.

cards.passage: The library closes at three the computer lab stays open until five.
cards.prompt: Where does the semicolon belong?
choices: after "closes"
after "three"
after "lab"
after "open"
cards.accept: "The library closes at three" and "the computer lab stays open until five" are both complete sentences; the semicolon goes between them.

cards.prompt: Which pair could be joined with a semicolon?
choices: Because the game ran late / we got home at midnight
After the game / the long drive home
The game ran late / we got home at midnight
The game ran late / and the drive home
cards.accept: Only C has a complete sentence on both sides. A starts with "because," so its first half can't stand alone.

cards.prompt: Which sentence punctuates the list correctly?
choices: We visited Utica, New York; Syracuse, New York; and Rochester, New York.
We visited Utica, New York, Syracuse, New York, and Rochester, New York.
cards.accept: When list items already contain commas, semicolons separate the items so readers can tell where each one ends.

cards.prompt: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
choices: Bring three things to the exam: a pencil, an eraser, and your ID.
Bring: a pencil, an eraser, and your ID.
cards.accept: A colon needs a complete sentence before it. "Bring" alone can't stand as a sentence.

cards.prompt: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
choices: The recipe needs: flour, sugar, and eggs.
The recipe needs three ingredients: flour, sugar, and eggs.
cards.accept: "The recipe needs" is incomplete without its object; "The recipe needs three ingredients" is a complete sentence.

cards.prompt: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
choices: Maya had one goal for the season; a spot on the varsity team.
Maya had one goal for the season: a spot on the varsity team.
cards.accept: What follows isn't a complete sentence, so a semicolon can't introduce it. A colon introduces the explanation.

cards.prompt: Which sentence uses a colon correctly?
choices: My favorite authors are: Stephen King and Jason Reynolds.
The forecast called for one thing: snow.
We left early because: the roads were bad.
The trip included: hiking, fishing, and canoeing.
cards.accept: Only B has a complete sentence before the colon. In A, C, and D, the colon splits a sentence in the middle.

cards.passage: The coach posted the starting lineup ___ Jordan, Kayla, Ben, Luis, and Mia.
cards.prompt: Which mark belongs in the blank?
choices: comma
semicolon
colon
no mark
cards.accept: "The coach posted the starting lineup" is complete, and the names that follow are the list it introduces.

cards.passage: The power went out at eight ___ it came back on at midnight.
cards.prompt: Which mark belongs in the blank?
choices: colon
comma
no mark
semicolon
cards.accept: Two complete sentences, and the second doesn't explain the first, so a semicolon joins them. A comma would make a comma splice.

cards.prompt: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
choices: I forgot my calculator; therefore, I borrowed one from Sam.
I forgot my calculator, therefore I borrowed one from Sam.
cards.accept: "Therefore" can't join two sentences by itself. Use a semicolon before it and a comma after it.

cards.prompt: Which sentence has a punctuation error?
choices: The fair opens Friday; tickets are five dollars.
We need two volunteers: one to sell tickets and one to park cars.
The barn was old; but it was still standing.
Bring the following: boots, gloves, and a hat.
cards.accept: With "but," use a comma: "old, but it was." A semicolon replaces the conjunction; it doesn't go with one.

cards.prompt: Which sentence uses a semicolon correctly?
choices: Although it rained; the game went on.
The game went on; although it rained.
It rained all afternoon; the game went on anyway.
It rained all afternoon; and the game went on.
cards.accept: "Although it rained" can't stand alone, so A and B are wrong. D adds "and," which needs a comma, not a semicolon.

cards.prompt: Which sentence is punctuated correctly?
choices: The finalists were Ava, a junior, Liam, a sophomore, and Noor, a senior.
The finalists were Ava, a junior; Liam, a sophomore; and Noor, a senior.
cards.accept: Each item already has a comma ("Ava, a junior"), so semicolons separate the three finalists. Without them it looks like six people.

cards.passage: The bridge was closed. Drivers took the long way.
cards.prompt: Which combines the two sentences correctly?
choices: The bridge was closed, drivers took the long way.
The bridge was closed: drivers, took the long way.
The bridge was closed; drivers took the long way.
The bridge was closed; and drivers took the long way.
cards.accept: A semicolon joins two complete sentences on its own. A is a comma splice; D adds "and."

cards.passage: We had one problem: the bus never came.
cards.prompt: Why is the colon correct here?
choices: It comes before a list.
It joins two sentences with "and."
It always follows the word "problem."
A complete sentence comes before it, and what follows explains it.
cards.accept: "We had one problem" is complete, and "the bus never came" explains what the problem was.

cards.passage: The tour stops in Albany, New York; Burlington, Vermont; and Boston, Massachusetts.
cards.prompt: Why does this list use semicolons?
choices: Each item is a complete sentence.
The list has more than two items.
City names always take semicolons.
The items already contain commas.
cards.accept: Each city-and-state item has its own comma, so semicolons mark where one item ends.

cards.passage: Jon works late, he rarely studies.
cards.prompt: Which revision is correct?
choices: Jon works late: and he rarely studies.
Jon works late; and he rarely studies.
Jon works late, he, rarely studies.
Jon works late; he rarely studies.
cards.accept: A semicolon joins the two complete sentences. A and B add "and" after the mark; C adds commas that don't belong.
